rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice when separate things are joined to form one whole.

example.english: Once we merge the two tables, there’ll be enough room to eat.
example.traditional: 將兩張枱合埋一齊，先夠位食飯。
example.jyutping: zoeng1 loeng5 zoeng1 ci4 hap6 maai4 jat1 cai4 sin1 gau3 wai6 sik6 faan6

rows.note: Use this when something gradually becomes part of its surrounding setting, group, or substance.

example.english: They quickly merge into the team at their new company.
example.traditional: 佢好快就融入新公司嘅團隊。
example.jyutping: keoi5 hou2 faai3 zau6 jung4 jap6 san1 gung1 si1 ge3 tyun4 deoi2

rows.note: Use this for a stream, road, or traffic lane flowing into another route or stream.

example.english: This lane will merge into the main road a little further ahead, so don't get into the wrong lane.
example.traditional: 呢條行車線再行前少少就會匯入主幹道，唔好揸錯線。
example.jyutping: ni1 tiu4 haang4 ce1 sin3 zoi3 haang4 cin4 siu2 siu2 zau6 wui6 wui6 jap6 zyu2 gon3 dou6 m4 hou2 zaa1 co3 sin3
